summary: Reviewed the seasonal dynamic-field flow, SSOT drift guard, SSOT structural changes, and the new Easter Sunday page for failure paths and partial-state issues. The main risk is around future stale event data and CTA override wiring, not crashes on empty or partial dynamic fields.
appears_sound: `resolveSeasonalFields` drops undefined, blank, and whitespace-only values before rendering, so partial dynamic-field payloads do not create empty rows in `lib/seasonal-utils.ts`.
`SeasonalDynamicDetails` returns `null` when `resolved.hasDetails` is false, so pages do not show an empty dynamic-details card in `components/seasonal/SeasonalDynamicDetails.tsx`.
The SSOT drift guard includes negative assertions for the old `20 guests` booking copy and banned customer-facing claims, making those tests materially meaningful in `tests/ssot-drift-guard.test.ts`.

findings.description: The Easter page hardcodes the schema event date to 2027 while the visible page is intended to be evergreen. Failure sequence: the site remains deployed after April 4, 2027, search engines and users see a scheduled Event that is already in the past, and the page appears stale even though the copy still reads evergreen.
findings.evidence: `EASTER_SUNDAY_DATE` is fixed to `'2027-04-04'`, and the JSON-LD always emits `EventScheduled` start/end dates from that constant in `app/easter-sunday/page.tsx:31`.
findings.why_it_might_be_wrong: The owner may intentionally want the page to target only Easter Sunday 2027 for this release cycle.
findings.what_would_confirm: Confirm whether this page is meant to auto-roll annually or whether a scheduled content update before April 4, 2027 is part of the release workflow.

findings.description: CTA override fields are resolved but no shown consumer applies them, so an annual update that only changes `ctaLabel` or `ctaDestination` would silently do nothing. Failure sequence: owner/API supplies a seasonal CTA override, resolver accepts it, the details block may render or not render based only on rows, and the page still sends users to the default booking CTA.
findings.evidence: `resolveSeasonalFields` returns `ctaLabel` and `ctaDestination`, but `SeasonalDynamicDetails` only checks `hasDetails` and renders `resolved.details` in `components/seasonal/SeasonalDynamicDetails.tsx:27`.
findings.why_it_might_be_wrong: Another page component outside the pack may consume `resolveSeasonalFields` directly and apply the CTA overrides.
findings.what_would_confirm: Check seasonal page templates for any direct use of `resolved.ctaLabel` or `resolved.ctaDestination`.

empty_categories: No double-submit, retry, or idempotency risks found in the changed code because the pack contains render-only/static build-time logic.
No partial-field crash path found in `SeasonalDynamicDetails`; empty and blank fields are filtered before rendering.
No SSOT removed-key consumer break is visible in the provided consumers; `HeroBadge` and `menu-page-data` read keys still present in the diff.
No JSON validity issue is visible in the provided SSOT diff.
